rationale: This record is a journal editorial (explicitly identified in the DOI `10.1590/1809-4422ASOCeditorialV1912016`) whose abstract text consists of introductory commentary reciting secondary global statistics from WHO, UNESCO, and IPCC on water scarcity, ecosystem degradation, and drinking water/sanitation disparities. It presents no primary empirical research or systematic review synthesis (failing Criterion 3, E05) and does not empirically evaluate a specific legal or administrative rule-type mechanism governing household water or sanitation access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain literal reading of Criterion 2 yield an exclude decision because the record is a non-empirical journal editorial (E05); additionally, under the narrow Criterion 2 reading, the text offers only broad macro-level human rights and SDG commentary rather than examining a specific legal or administrative mechanism.

evidence_quotes.quote: In many countries, including Brazil, the disparities in water and sanitation services are among the main battlefronts when projecting a fairer and more sustainable society, according to 2015 UNESCO data.
Approximately 80% of the world suffers severe threats regarding hydric security, according to IPCC indicators, concerning water availability, demand, and pollution.
